name: Edge and on-device AI
summary: AI runs locally on phones, PCs, cameras and industrial equipment to reduce latency and reliance on a cloud connection.
useCase: A factory camera detects a defective component immediately on the production line; a laptop transcribes a confidential meeting locally.
whyNow: Specialized neural processors are spreading through devices while smaller models improve the range of feasible local tasks. Hardware availability is moving faster than evidence of daily use. Counterpoint counted 143 generative-AI-capable smartphone models in Q1 2025, up from 123 one quarter earlier. IoT Analytics still estimated that fewer than 1% of connected IoT devices contained a true AI accelerator at the end of 2025.

mainstream.scope: Routine useful local AI on premium-to-midrange PCs and phones, plus selected industrial edge devices; not every connected sensor.
mainstream.rationale: A normal device replacement cycle can distribute capable hardware rapidly, and Gartner expected AI PCs to become standard by 2029. Adoption of useful applications may lag the installed chips. Memory costs, battery life and weaker-than-expected PC demand could delay the window, especially outside premium markets.

metric.name: GenAI-capable smartphone models tracked
metric.growthLabel: +20 capable models between Q4 2024 and Q1 2025
metric.limitations: Supply-side model count, not shipment volume, installed base or active AI feature use. Two quarterly snapshots, not annual totals. Devices differ substantially in local model capability. There is no fabricated continuous 2021–2026 adoption series.
metric.futureNote: Gartner’s separately displayed PC forecast concerns a different device class and was published in August 2025, before the 2026 memory-market shock.

outlookMetrics.name: AI PC shipments
outlookMetrics.note: Forecast of 55% of PC shipments. Not an observed 2026 result and not directly comparable with smartphone model counts.

maturity.note: Analyst ordinal assessment, not an adoption percentage: 0 research, 1 proof of concept, 2 pilots, 3 commercial niche, 4 routine use in the stated market, 5 established/expanding. Future values are a scenario.

milestones.text: No comparable generative edge-AI adoption measure identified; earlier mobile neural processing had different workloads.
No comparable local-generative-AI usage count identified.
IDC identified the first next-generation AI smartphones in the second half of 2023.
Counterpoint’s year-end catalog contained 123 GenAI-capable smartphone models.
The catalog reached 143 models in Q1; true edge accelerators remained rare across the broader IoT base.
IDC highlighted memory-related PC and smartphone constraints; Microchip completed its acquisition of Hailo in September.

tailwinds: Low-latency and offline operation create clear value for cameras, machinery and mobile interfaces.
Local processing can reduce cloud traffic and keep selected sensitive inputs on the device.
bottlenecks: Memory bandwidth, heat, power and model size limit useful local workloads.
A capable NPU can remain idle if applications do not provide a compelling recurring use case.
watchMetrics: Active local-inference users and workload share, rather than device marketing labels.
Cost and energy per useful inference, measured at the required accuracy and latency.
